hints: Remember what makes a carbon chiral, it must be joined to four completely different groups.
Since this is an alkane, the only groups available are H and alkyl groups, so try using H plus three different alkyl groups to keep the total small.
Test the smallest alkyl groups, methyl, ethyl and propyl, on one central carbon and count up all the carbons including the central one.
walkthrough:
**Recall the chiral centre rule**

A chiral centre is a carbon with four different groups attached to it. For an alkane, those groups can only be $\text{H}$ or alkyl groups like $\text{CH}_3$, $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5$.

Rule:
$$\text{chiral C} = \text{C with 4 different substituents}$$

**Choose the cheapest way to get four different groups**

Using $\text{H}$ as one group is smartest, because then you only need three different alkyl groups. Without $\text{H}$ you would need four different alkyl groups, which uses many more carbons.

**Build the smallest possible example**

Pick the three smallest different alkyl groups: methyl ($\text{CH}_3$, 1 C), ethyl ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2$, 2 C) and propyl ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2$, 3 C). Attach them plus $\text{H}$ to a central carbon.

Total carbons:
$$1 \text{ (central)} + 1 + 2 + 3 = 7$$

**Check it works and cannot be smaller**

This molecule is 3-methylhexane, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$, and the C-3 is chiral. You cannot do it with 6 carbons because the third alkyl group would have to repeat methyl or ethyl, so 7 is the least possible.

options.A: Correct. A central carbon joined to H, methyl (1 C), ethyl (2 C) and propyl (3 C) gives 1 + 1 + 2 + 3 = 7 carbons. This is 3-methylhexane, which has a genuine chiral centre at C-3.
options.B: Incorrect. 8 carbons can certainly be chiral, for example 3-methylheptane, but it is not the least number. Students choosing this often think the propyl group must be branched, adding an extra carbon unnecessarily.
options.C: Incorrect. 9 or more carbons is larger than needed. This choice may come from trying to use four alkyl groups with no H, which needs many more carbons, instead of using the efficient H plus three alkyl groups route.
options.D: Incorrect. 10 carbons is the minimum if the chiral carbon has no H and is joined to four different alkyl groups (methyl, ethyl, n-propyl, isopropyl). But allowing H gives a much smaller chiral alkane, so 10 is not the least.
